messages.content: The Atlanta clinic finally answered. Thursday room access is 4:45 to 6, they can wrap Friday by 3 if I keep the debrief tight, and they have a locked workroom for my kit during lunch. Can we turn Plan A into an actual booking? Check whether the 6:20 return is still sane before you click anything.

Yes, the 6:20 p.m. ATL-TPA return is practical, not plush. If you leave the clinic by 3:20, the rideshare estimate to ATL is 40-60 minutes, which puts you at the airport around 4:15-4:25. The risk is Friday traffic if the debrief slips past 3:15. The Saturday 1:25 p.m. return is easier but adds another hotel night and part of Saturday.

Current pieces: Thu Nov 7 TPA-ATL nonstop 11:10 a.m.-12:42 p.m.; Fri Nov 8 ATL-TPA nonstop 6:20-7:52 p.m.; airfare is $236 main cabin. Suite hotel is available Nov 7-8 in a cancellable queen studio at $184 plus tax. It has the coffee maker, mini-fridge, desk, and fitness room confirmed. Still no pool or hot tub.
That sounds workable. I do not want to add Saturday unless Friday is genuinely too tight. How much more is Saturday?

Saturday would add about $217 for the extra hotel night after tax, and the Saturday afternoon fare is $48 more right now. So Plan B costs roughly $265 more and buys comfort margin, not a better work schedule. Since they confirmed storage and a 3 p.m. wrap, I would book the Friday 6:20 as long as you treat 3:20 as your hard clinic departure.
Book Friday then. Use the suite hotel. Window seat if you can, but do not pay extra for it.

I can get included window seats on both legs: 17F on the outbound and 18A on the return. Before I purchase: this is main cabin, not refundable for cash, but it can be changed for airline credit under the fare rules. Carry-on is included. The hotel is cancellable until 6 p.m. local time on Nov 5, and late checkout would be only a request. Confirm I should purchase the flights and reserve the room?
Confirmed.
Flights are booked. Confirmation ATL-MOB-8846: Thu Nov 7, TPA 11:10 a.m. to ATL 12:42 p.m., seat 17F; Fri Nov 8, ATL 6:20 p.m. to TPA 7:52 p.m., seat 18A. Total airfare charged: $236.
Good. Book the suite and ask for late checkout Friday if they will note it.

Suite hotel is reserved. Confirmation DEC-SUITE-5092 for Nov 7-8: queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, work desk, and fitness room confirmed. No pool or hot tub at this property. Late checkout for Friday is attached as a request, not guaranteed. Room total is $211.38 after tax, cancellable until Nov 5 at 6 p.m.
Let's keep rideshare instead of a rental, right?

Yes. Rideshare is simpler here. The hotel has limited parking, the clinic is only about 10 minutes away, and you do not need a car during teaching. Plan: airport to hotel Thursday around 1 p.m.; hotel to clinic around 4:10 for the 4:45 room access; hotel to clinic Friday morning; clinic to ATL no later than 3:20 p.m.
Send me the confirmations and the watch list plainly.

Sent. Booked Atlanta plan: flights ATL-MOB-8846, hotel DEC-SUITE-5092. Watch items: Friday return depends on leaving the clinic by 3:20; keep the debrief focused so the 3 p.m. wrap holds; late checkout is requested but not guaranteed; hotel has fitness but no pool or hot tub; keep the kit in the locked workroom only during the confirmed lunch window; use rideshare rather than renting unless the clinic changes parking expectations.

messages.content: After Atlanta, I want one non-work thing on the calendar. Dan and I are looking at Tucson for a hiking and recovery weekend in early December. Can you compare Thursday after work versus Friday morning out of Tampa, plus hotel zones? Please group it by practical choice, not just cheapest.

Sure. Are you thinking Thu Dec 5-Mon Dec 9 if you leave Thursday, or Fri Dec 6-Mon Dec 9 if you leave Friday? And are the likely hikes Sabino Canyon/Catalina Foothills/Saguaro, or more of a downtown food-and-easy-trails trip?
Yes on those dates. Two adults. More Sabino/Catalina and maybe Saguaro than downtown. Monday return should be afternoon if possible. I do not want to land at 1 a.m. and be useless Tuesday.

Best flight patterns right now:

Most practical: Thu after work, TPA 4:55 p.m. to TUS 9:38 p.m. via DFW, then Mon TUS 12:35 p.m. to TPA 8:46 p.m. via DFW. About $486 per person. You get all of Friday for hiking.

Cheapest-ish but less useful: Fri late afternoon departure, arrives Tucson close to midnight, then same Monday return. About $418 per person, but Friday is basically lost.

Friday morning practical option: TPA around 8:20 a.m., arrives TUS mid-afternoon. About $535 per person. Better than midnight, but it still eats half of Friday and costs more than Thursday.
So Thursday may actually be the cleanest. For lodging, hot tub and fitness matter on this one. We are going to be sore.

Then I would shortlist it this way:

1. Foothills resort near Sabino/Catalina: strongest recovery setup. 4.5 guest rating, pool, hot tub, fitness room, in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge. Closest to the hikes. Downsides: resort fee, parking charge, and you will want a rental car.

2. Downtown hotel: better for walking to dinner and cheaper nightly rate. 4.2 rating, fitness room and pool, but no hot tub and smaller rooms. Trail drives are longer.

3. Trailhead casita: most private, kitchenette, quiet location near trails. But ratings are sparse, no fitness room, no shared pool/hot tub, and cancellation rules are stricter.
Put real totals next to those. Resort fees always make the first quote fake.

For Thu-Mon, four nights, before flights:

Foothills resort: $219 average nightly rate, about $988 with tax, plus $39 nightly resort fee and $18 nightly parking. Lodging total about $1,216. Rental car estimate: $246 for a midsize, so ground/lodging total about $1,462.

Downtown hotel: $156 average nightly rate, about $704 with tax. No resort fee; parking is included. You would still want a car for the hikes, so with the same rental it is about $950.

Trailhead casita: $185 average nightly rate plus cleaning/service fees, about $1,024 total. Car needed. Ground/lodging total about $1,270.
Does downtown actually let us skip the rental car?

Not for the trip you described. Downtown helps with dinner and coffee, but rideshares to trailheads can be spotty early and annoying after hikes. For Sabino/Catalina plus Saguaro, a rental is the practical call for all three lodging choices.
Okay. What are the Monday returns that are actually civilized?

Three usable Monday returns:

Best balance: TUS 12:35 p.m. via DFW, arrive TPA 8:46 p.m. Good cushion after checkout and not brutal Tuesday.

Later but still okay: TUS 1:50 p.m. via DEN, arrive TPA 10:12 p.m. More breathing room in the morning, later home.

Too late for my taste here: TUS 3:05 p.m. via ATL, arrive TPA 11:38 p.m. It is afternoon, but it makes Tuesday rougher.
Use the 12:35 as the comparison point. No need to preserve Monday morning for a big hike.

Then the practical flight plan is Thursday 4:55 p.m. out of Tampa and Monday 12:35 p.m. out of Tucson. It costs more than the ugly Friday-night arrival, but it protects Friday, keeps Monday reasonable, and avoids paying extra for the Friday-morning itinerary that still lands mid-afternoon.
How much worse is the resort total once flights are included?

Using the Thursday flight plan for two people at about $972 total airfare:

Foothills resort plus car: about $2,434 all-in.
Downtown hotel plus car: about $1,922 all-in.
Trailhead casita plus car: about $2,242 all-in.

So the resort is roughly $512 more than downtown and $192 more than the casita. The resort is the only one that cleanly checks pool, hot tub, fitness, room fridge/coffee, and close-to-trails. Downtown is the value pick if you can give up the hot tub.
The casita sounds nice, but sparse ratings on a short trip makes me nervous.

I would treat the casita as a privacy gamble, not the safest practical choice. It could be great, but the limited review base and lack of fitness/recovery amenities make it harder to justify when the trip is only four nights.
Can you check whether the resort's standard room really has a queen, mini-fridge, and coffee maker? I do not want to pay resort pricing and then fight the room setup.

The resort's standard desert queen room lists one queen bed, coffee maker, mini-fridge, and small table/desk. Pool is open 7 a.m.-10 p.m.; hot tub 8 a.m.-10 p.m.; fitness room 24 hours. Caveat: the quoted room does not include breakfast, and the resort fee plus parking are separate from the nightly rate.
Hold off on booking. Dan needs to confirm he can leave Thursday after work. If he can, I am leaning resort even though it is not the bargain.

No booking made. Working recommendation: Thu Dec 5 after-work departure, Mon Dec 9 12:35 p.m. return, foothills resort, and a midsize rental car. Value fallback is downtown if the total starts feeling too high, but it gives up the hot tub and adds trail-driving time. Open items: Dan confirms Thursday availability, then I should recheck airfare, resort fee/parking total, room cancellation deadline, and seat options before purchase.

messages.content: Dan can leave Thursday. Let's book Tucson if the total has not gotten silly. I want the resort, but re-check the fees before I commit.

Current total is slightly higher but still in the same lane. Flights: Thu Dec 5 TPA 4:55 p.m. to TUS 9:38 p.m. via DFW; Mon Dec 9 TUS 12:35 p.m. to TPA 8:46 p.m. via DFW. Airfare is $493 per person, $986 total.

Resort: queen desert room for four nights, $219 average nightly, $996.44 with tax. Separate fees: $39 nightly resort fee and $18 nightly parking, adding $228. Hotel total becomes $1,224.44. Midsize rental car is $246 pay-later. Full trip estimate: $2,456.44.
Higher than I wanted, but acceptable. What car category makes sense? We are not doing anything off-road.

A midsize car is enough for Sabino Canyon, Catalina Foothills trailheads, and Saguaro parking areas. A compact SUV is $74 more and only worth it if you want extra cargo height or change to rougher roads. I would book the midsize pay-later rate with free cancellation.
Midsize car. What do the seat maps look like?

Outbound has good included adjacent pairs with one window: TPA-DFW 21A/21B and DFW-TUS 18A/18B. Return is less ideal: included adjacent seats are aisle-middle pairs, TUS-DFW 16B/16C and DFW-TPA 23B/23C. To get adjacent window-middle pairs on the return would be $34 per seat per leg, so $136 total.
Take the outbound window pairs. Return keep us adjacent and free. I do not care $136 worth after the resort fees.

Understood. Before I book: airfare is main cabin and nonrefundable to cash, but changeable for airline credit under fare rules. Outbound seats include one window in each pair; return seats will be adjacent aisle-middle with no window unless something opens later. Resort is cancellable until Nov 28 at 6 p.m.; resort fee and parking are real add-ons, not optional if you have the car. Confirm flights, resort, and midsize rental?
Confirm.

Booked. Flights confirmation TUS-AIR-4471: Thu Dec 5 TPA-DFW-TUS 4:55 p.m.-9:38 p.m., seats 21A/21B and 18A/18B. Mon Dec 9 TUS-DFW-TPA 12:35 p.m.-8:46 p.m., seats 16B/16C and 23B/23C. Airfare charged: $986.

Resort confirmation FTH-RES-2380: Dec 5-9 queen desert room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool 7 a.m.-10 p.m., hot tub 8 a.m.-10 p.m., fitness room 24 hours. Hotel total including resort fee and parking estimate: $1,224.44.

Rental confirmation CAR-TUS-7719: midsize car, pay at pickup, estimated $246.
Please add a late-arrival note for Thursday and give me a Monday checkout plan.

Late-arrival note added to the resort reservation with expected arrival around 10:15-10:30 p.m. Monday plan: check out by 9:45 a.m., drive to TUS, return the rental by 10:35, and be inside the terminal around 10:50 for the 12:35 departure. That leaves room for gas, rental return, and security without making the morning frantic.
Send Dan just the itinerary, not every caveat. Send me the full version.

Done. Dan got the compact itinerary with flights, resort, car pickup, and Monday departure timing. You got the full confirmation packet. Watch items for you: resort cancellation deadline is Nov 28 at 6 p.m.; resort fee and parking are included in the estimate but charged separately on-site; return seats are adjacent aisle-middle with no window for now; rental is pay-later, so we can still change the car category if the hiking plan changes.
